utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al. Thank you, Your Honours much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. This is Tuesday, September 29th, 2009, and I greet the accused, members of the -- the counsel for Defence, all members of the OTP, and everyone helping us. I believe that the Registrar has an IC number for us.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Some parties have submitted lists of documents to be tendered through Witness Zvonimir Skender. The list submitted by 3D shall be given Exhibit IC1055, the list submitted by 2D shall be given Exhibit IC105 -- sorry, the previous number is actually 1053, and the list submitted by 2D shall be given Exhibit IC1054, and the list submitted by the OTP shall be given Exhibit IC1055. If I can take that again, the list submitted by 3D shall be given Exhibit IC1053, and the list submitted by 2D shall be given Exhibit IC1054, while the list submitted by the OTP shall be given Exhibit IC1055. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Let's bring the witness into the courtroom. Could the usher please go and get him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please give us your last name, first name, and date of birth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Zrinko Tokic, and I was born on the 18th of October, 1960.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is your current occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am a professor of defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where do you work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the profession I once did. I was in school, I taught at school, but I'm retired now and receive a military pension.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You receive a military pension. Could you tell us what your rank was when you left -- before you retired?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right, Your Honour. I retired as a brigadier in 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you already testified in court or is this the first time you're testifying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please read the solemn declaration on the card.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You may sit down. You have been called by the Defence, and you will be answering questions put to you by the Defence counsels first. Please try and be very specific in your answers. If you do not understand a question, just ask the person putting it to you to reformulate it. The four Judges on the Bench can also ask questions. It will all depend of -- on your answers and also mainly of documents that we will be shown. And then after the examination-in-chief, we'll have the cross-examination by the Prosecution. After that, there might be some redirect. You have been scheduled to be testifying all week, until Thursday. You have taken the oath. You're now a witness of justice. You're not supposed to contact the Defence any longer, so for the few evenings that you'll spend in The Hague, please be very silent and do not tell anyone what you've been testifying about, especially not to the media. Of course, you can talk with your relatives to tell them that -- to tell them what's going on, but don't contact the media. I wanted to say all this to make sure that this hearing would run as smoothly as possible. For some technical reasons, we break every hour and a half for 20 minutes, usually. Of course, if at any moment you feel poorly, just raise your hand and we'll have a break. I see that Ms. Alaburic has her lectern, she's ready, so we'll give her the floor immediately.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to you, too, Mr. Tokic. Good morning to the Prosecutor and everybody else in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tokic, during the proofing session we discussed your life, your CV, and we'd like to place on the ELMO your curriculum vitae. And I'd like to ask the usher's help for us to do that. The Trial Chamber has your CV, and I've handed a copy over to the Prosecutor, and I think we'll save some ten minutes if we put it on the ELMO and are able to look through it quickly. Mr. Tokic, tell us, you've seen your CV. Just tell us whether it corresponds to the basic information you provided us about your education, career, and other aspects of your life.

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Counsel, this CV is completely accurate and corresponds to what I told you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Would you then sign the documents and place today's date there, which is the 29th of September, 2009. And I'd like an IC number for the document after that, please. Thank you. If you have a pen, you can sign the paper to your right.

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And an IC number now, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The witness's CV shall be given Exhibit IC1056. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tokic, I'm just going to ask you some brief questions about your CV. It says here that in December 1997, you performed the duties of commander of the HVO for the Military District of Tomislavgrad, and my question to you is: Is it the same HVO that existed in 1992 and 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. During my professional career, in 1997 I was appointed commander of the Tomislavgrad Military District, as a component part of the Croatian Defence Council, in the army of the federation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You mean the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina; right?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It also says here that from October 2005 you were deputy chief, then chief of the municipality of Gornji Vakuf-Uskoplje. Can you tell us who appointed you to that post?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: After I had completed my professional career as a soldier, an opportunity presented itself for me to work in the Uskoplje-Gornji Vakuf municipality, and quite simply, as the OHR saw to the integration of two municipalities, Uskoplje and Gornji Vakuf, I was appointed in 2001 to the position of deputy chief, and Mr. Zero [phoen] Dragisa was appointed chief, but we rotated and took up that position every year.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The abbreviation you mentioned was not recorded. It was OHR, right, the abbreviation you mentioned? Can you tell us whether the OHR appointed you to that post?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: No. The transitional municipal council for the Gornji Vakuf-Uskoplje municipality, with 39 councillors, and this transitory municipal council had 23 Bosniaks, 16 -- and 16 Croats. And by general acclamation, that is to say, unanimously, they lifted up their hands to vote me in for that position.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, did the representatives of the Bosniaks vote for you too?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Yes, all 23 councillors from the Bosniak people voted to have me elected.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you just tell us briefly, Mr. Tokic, what OHR stands for? What is OHR?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: It is the Office of the High Commissioner, who, in Bosnia and Herzegovina, coordinated, quite simply -- coordinated within Bosnia-Herzegovina when the domestic politicians were not able to resolve something. Then the high commissioner had supreme authority and was able to make the decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, is that the representative of the international community; is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Yes, he is a representative of the international community.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, tell us, please, Mr. Tokic, during the conflict with the BH Army in 1993, did you attend a celebration of the BH Army of some kind on the territory of Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: After the January conflict, at the invitation of Mr. Okrakin [phoen] Agic and Fikret Musa for Army Day, which was the 15th of April, 1993, I was present at the cultural centre for these festivities and for commemorating Army Day, and I addressed everybody present on behalf of the HVO, everybody present in the hall, and I congratulated them on Army Day and said what their duties would be in the period to come.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right, fine. Thank you. Now, in your CV, Mr. Tokic, you say that you were never prosecuted. Now, do you have any knowledge that at the present time in Bosnia-Herzegovina there are criminal proceedings against you with respect to the events of January 1993 in the area of Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Well, with respect to communication with my soldiers and friends from the Bosniak people, with my communications with them, I have information that investigators are investigating my role in those events, the events of 1993, but for the moment I haven't had any official confirmation of that. But that is what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tokic, you did not seek any protective measures to testify here in The Hague. Can you explain to us why that is?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Well, I have no need to ask for protective measures. Everything I did, as an officer of the Croatian Defence Council, I did in conformity with the rules and regulations, so I have nothing to be ashamed of or to be afraid of, and for those reasons I consider that I don't need protection of any kind.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So we see once again from your CV that already in 1992, you were the commander, first of all, of the Municipal Staff of the HVO and then of the brigade, of a brigade. Can you tell us, Mr. Tokic, how the army was organised, the HVO army was organised at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Well, the army, the HVO, was organised at the beginning into municipal staffs pursuant to a decision of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna dated the 8th of April, 1992. And after receiving orders for the establishment of brigades, the brigades were, indeed, established, and that was -- that whole process was to be completed by September 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: According to what principle?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly slow down and pause between question and answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The brigade was organised according to the territorial principle.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you explain, taking the example of Gornji Vakuf, what that means in practice?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: It meant that for the Gornji Vakuf-Uskoplje municipality, the Dr. Ante Starcevic Brigade is the brigade covering that territory, and it has its mobilisational deployment and is made up of military conscripts from the Gornji Vakuf area.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly slow down for the record. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In line 19 -- yes, everything is there, the full name of the brigade. Now, take a look at the next document, please. It is an excerpt from the Territorial Division of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It is a Prosecution document, and we're interested in the Gornji Vakuf municipality for the time being. Can you, Mr. Tokic, tell us, in 1992, what area of Gornji Vakuf municipality was your brigade active in and what did it do there?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: The Dr. Ante Starcevic Brigade held the defence line facing the Army of Republika Srpska on Mount Radus so that it organised the front-line in such a way as to ensure that Radus and the Rama Brigade, to its left, and its neighbouring Eugen Kvaternik Brigade on the right, acted along that line.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: That second brigade that you mentioned, you said Eugen Kvaternik Brigade; right?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Eugen, E-u-g-e-n, Kvaternik, K-v -- et cetera, we'll put that right later on. But, Mr. Tokic, could you draw on that map where the line was, the line held by your brigade in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: No, you're drawing in the line at Bugojno.

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: I apologise, but my brigade, in 1992, held part of the line in Gornji Vakuf-Uskoplje municipality and part of the line in the Bugojno municipality area.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Sir, what about the border between Gornji Vakuf and Kupres, the one that you marked now? Was that an area in which your brigade was active, the relatively short border, Gornji Vakuf-Kupres?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I directly deployed my brigade along the defence line covering the border area between Gornji Vakuf, Uskoplje, and Kupres municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And in addition to the front-line, itself, did your brigade have an area of combat activity in Gornji Vakuf town, itself, or anywhere deeper into the territory of Gornji Vakuf municipality?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Mr. Tokic, let me interrupt you. You have already been asked by the interpreters and also by Maitre Alaburic that you have to wait after the questions and you have to wait for the interpreters, and then to start with your answer. Please kindly cooperate on this matter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tokic, my question was: What about deeper into the territory of Gornji Vakuf and Gornji Vakuf town, itself, back in 1992. Was that to an area in which your brigade was carrying out combat activities back in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: My unit was defending the front-line. The front-line is what it says, the front-line, as well as settlements deeper into the territory behind the front-line. When we soldiers use that expression, when we say "a task to be carried out deeper into the territory," we normally mean about three kilometres' deep. The line to the light [as interpreted] was Raduski Kamen, to the right Srpski Brdo, and then further into the territory, the Voljice settlement.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tokic, can you please mark today's date on this map and sign the map, please. And if we can please have a number for the map as well.

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the map just marked by the witness shall be given Exhibit IC1057. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The next map, Mr. Tokic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me. I would like you, Mr. Tokic, to clearly answer the question of counsel. Did you have troops of your brigade in Gornji Vakuf, itself, or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The command post of my brigade, Your Honour, was in Gornji Vakuf-Uskoplje, only elements of command. All my units in defensive activities were brought to the front-lines facing the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: And I would suppose you had a small group of soldiers for the protection of the command post; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there was a security platoon at the command post, a solid security unit, for the purposes of the command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tokic, another question about this.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note: Could counsel please move closer to the microphone. We can't hear her properly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In 1993 -- it appears that someone else's microphone is on, not being used. Mr. Tokic, let us try to be specific about this and tell the Chamber what our position is, what your position is, regarding the area of combat activity of your brigade in January 1993, during the clashes with the BH Army. Where was the front-line at the time during those clashes?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: The Dr. Ante Starcevic Brigade was at the time holding a defence line facing the VRS from two different directions along which logistical assistance was arriving. One of them was Raduski Kamen-Oglavak-Nisan, and logistical assistance was arriving down the Gornji Vakuf-Doljica [phoen]-Radus line. The other line was Humac-Vukova Glava-Skrtsko Brdo, down the depth, down the depth, Jazvenik. The logistical assistance was arriving from Gornji Vakuf, Uskoplje, Gracanica, Kordici, Jazvenik.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us briefly, without detailed place names, what the front-line was facing the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: The front-line facing the BH Army was the entire area of Gornji Vakuf-Uskoplje municipality, where the forces of the Dr. Ante Starcevic Brigade were deployed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tokic, at the time the entire municipality, in a way, became an area of combat activity. You, as the commander of the municipal brigade, would have assumed the powers normally associated with civilian authorities; would that have been the case?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Most certainly not.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Fine. I would now like to go back to this chart regarding the position of Gornji Vakuf. Could you please tell us what the significance of Gornji Vakuf was, in terms of traffic connections, if any?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Geographically speaking, Gornji Vakuf-Uskoplje municipality constituted a link between Central Bosnia and Herzegovina. Many people say that the area constitutes a gate to Central Bosnia. For that reason, it has an exceptional significance for all people living in Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. Can we move on to the next map, please. The map shows the Gornji Vakuf-Uskoplje municipal territory, the situation as it was on the 8th of January, 1993. Marked in blue, we see the territory held by the Croats, and marked by green the territory held by the Muslims, which to a large extent tallied with the population in these two respective areas. Mr. Tokic, was this map drawn based on your instructions? Were you, essentially, the person who drew this map?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Madam, while preparing my evidence here, I produced this map.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Fine. I think we best just explain to the Chamber right away about the portions that are important to us. Next to place names mentioned in the indictment, we have the village of Zdrimci on this and map marked in green, meaning it was BH Army held. The BH Army was in that village. Would that be right, Mr. Tokic?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Madam, Zdrimci is a mixed village with both Croats and Bosniaks living there. Right in the middle of the village, there is simply a higher concentration of Bosniak population.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: We need to spell the name correctly, since it's important and it's mentioned in the indictment. Zdrimci. Mr. Tokic, were there any BH Army units in that village or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me, Ms. Alaburic. I cannot help noticing that the spelling on the map is different from the one that we have on the transcript. It is Zdrimci with an M like "Maria" and not an N, like "Nicholas"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The letter is M, but we've tried to correct the name several times and we failed, so we simply took down the reference to get it corrected later on. Z-d-r-i-m-c-i. The first letter is a Z, like "Zagreb," yes, actually "zh," which doesn't exist in the English language. Be that as it may, the name on the map is correct, and we find the same name on the indictment. Therefore, there is no problem with that. All right. And now the same question in relation to the villages of Dusa and Uzricje, and Uzricje. That's right, fine, it's been entered correctly. Were there any BH Army units in those villages?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: In those villages, too, there were organised BH Army units.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tokic, could you please indicate Hrasnica on the map?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Hrasnica, in relation to Gornji Vakuf municipality, is eight kilometres towards Bugojno.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Were there any BH Army units in that area as well?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: In Hrasnica itself, there were some organised BH Army units?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The Hrasnica area, if we looked closely at it, we see that the area controlled by the Croats is cut across by a BH Army-held corridor. Could you tell us which road runs through that area from Uskoplje towards the north?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Madam counsel, the road connecting Gornji Vakuf, Uskoplje, and Bugojno, this is M-62, and it runs just there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tokic, could you underline the Hrasnica area? Just circle it. It doesn't matter what it ends up looking like.

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Fine. Can you please mark the road to Bugojno, cut across by this Muslim-controlled corridor?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You'll be given a better marker.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me. I would like to ask a question. Witness, you made this map, and in the map there is a no-man's zone, as it were, in my view, the white area. Counsel, however, says that that area was Muslim no -- yes, Muslim controlled, I think. Could you clarify, if counsel is right, why, then, did you leave it this white?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, when units go to the field, they take up certain lines within this area, and there is an area of firing -- small-arms firing within that area. For that reason, any army approaching a position there would very much make sure they didn't put their men in harm's way. This was a buffer zone that was created for that reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: As a buffer zone, wouldn't it be controlled, in a way, by -- from both sides?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tokic, tell us, please, this area coloured green that I referred to, so it is the green area that cuts across the Gornji Vakuf-Bugojno line, was that territory that was Muslim held?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Counsel, you're absolutely right, that was the area controlled by the Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just give an explanation to Judge Trechsel. My question referred to the area which is coloured in, not the area which is left without colour. And that would have been my next question, but the witness has already told us that it was a buffer zone.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Tokic, could you sign this map, too, with today's date, and then I'd like to ask for an IC number for the map.

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, can we have an IC number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The second map just marked by the witness shall be given Exhibit IC1058. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And now, Mr. Tokic, the last little map that we have prepared for you and that you were shown during the proofing session, it shows the area of the town of Gornji Vakuf, itself. It's an old map, so it does not show all the buildings and facilities that were built after this map was compiled 30 years ago. Anyway, Mr. Tokic, it serves its purpose. Did you draw this map in preparation for your testimony here today?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did draw this map.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: On this map, we have a group of facilities and buildings and the MUP building, because these are mentioned separately in the indictment. So, Mr. Tokic, I'm first of all going to ask you about these factories in the industrial zone. When did the HVO and your brigade come into possession of those facilities?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Counsel, the Dr. Ante Starcevic Brigade took control of these facilities in the second conflict on the 23rd of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, how long were these facilities under the control of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: We based -- were based in these facilities until the 27th of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Do I understand you correctly, that's four days?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, was there any fighting going on with the BH Army over those facilities at all?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Counsel, we didn't need to fight for those facilities because my units -- the men in my units live next to these factories, so we didn't have to fight for them with anyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And did the BH Army have any units of its own in those factories?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: The BH Army never had any of its units in those factories.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, the MUP building, how did the HVO come to control the MUP building?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: The Ante Starcevic Brigade's units, in a conflict on the 24th of October, managed to take control of the MUP building.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: When you say "took," what do you mean? It implies some combat, does it not, if you take a building?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: When the clash broke out between the BH Army and the Dr. Ante Starcevic Brigade in the municipality of Gornji Vakuf, and that was in October 1992, what happened then was that the units of the Ante Starcevic Brigade reached this position, the building, to stop the further advance of the BH Army towards the area where the Dr. Starcevic Brigade was organised.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, was the building empty or were there BH Army soldiers inside, or some civilians, perhaps, or anybody else?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: There was nobody in the building. The facility -- well, we took control of the facility without any fighting.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right, thank you. We've completed that introductory part, but let's just round it off. There's an incident mentioned with a flag in the indictment at the beginning of January 19 -- can you tell us, Mr. Tokic, what flag, whose flag? What was this flag which led to this armed incident?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Counsel, it was the flags of the Croatian nation in Bosnia-Herzegovina, and those flags were hoisted for Christmas, the biggest Catholic religious feast.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting you, but the date was January 1993? I'm not asking about Christmas 1992, but the incident which led to an armed intervention of this kind. It didn't have any major consequences, but just tell us who hoisted what flag which led to the incident breaking out.

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: In January 1993, members of HOS, H-O-S, on a lamp post in the street, raised a HOS flag.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And was it that flag which gave rise to the incident that followed?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, the flag caused the incident.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, and I'd like to thank the usher, too. We're done with the maps, and we'll move on to documents. I do apologise. I need a number for the document, so would you sign your name there, too, please, with today's date, and then may we have an IC number for this document. And I'd like to thank Mr. Kovacic, my colleague, for reminding me of that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The third map just marked by the witness shall be given Exhibit IC1059. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's now try, Mr. Tokic, to get through the documents as quickly as possible, and I'll probably reduce the list. The first document that you have, in my set of documents, is 4D1667. It is a command -- an order from Zeljko Siljeg, dated September 1992. Tell us, please, Mr. Tokic, are you familiar with the document? Did you receive it in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Madam, I am familiar with this document, and I did receive it on the date specified.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Siljeg mentions a possible attack by the Chetniks on Bugojno. Tell us, please, in September 1992 were there, indeed, battles with the Army of Republika Srpska or the Chetniks, or whatever we want to call them? So what I'm asking you is: Is what it says in the document correct?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Counsel, a little before this document was written, an attack was stopped against our defence lines, and this document is a warning to us, telling us that the Army of Republika Srpska wants to continue attacking our lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Now, in point 3 of this document, Colonel Siljeg is asking for cooperation between the HVO and the TO or, rather, the BH Army. Tell us, please, did the HVO and BH Army cooperate and join forces in fighting a common enemy when this order was issued?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Counsel, when this order was issued, along the defence lines facing the Army of Republika Srpska, the lines were jointly held by the Dr. Ante Starcevic Brigade and the 317th Brigade of the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's move on to the next document, which is 4D --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to discuss the fourth paragraph that is before us. On reading it, one has the feeling that according to a number of reports coming from the intelligence services, the Serbs would have infiltrated some troops who would be working to generate a conflict between the HVO and the Territorial Defence, and the Territorial Defence is represented here by the Muslims. I tried to visualise the following situation: If the Serbs sent some of their men in depth who are dressed in camouflage uniforms and who, over night, infiltrate the ABiH lines and shoot at the HVO, the HVO may believe that Muslims are firing at them, or vice versa -- or, vice versa, the Serbs infiltrate the HVO lines and fire at the Muslims, and the Muslims have every reason to believe that the HVO are firing at them. This situation, i.e., infiltration by the Serbs, was this something you actually witnessed with your own eyes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I be allowed to explain and say that in June 1992, the 8th of June, in actual fact, there was an ambush along the approach to Raduski Kamen, and in that ambush my assistant -- artillery assistant, Hajrudin Salihovic, was killed, and the chief of my operations department, [indiscernible], too, the commander of the 120th, too, and the line linking the HVO and Bugojno municipality, Gornji Vakuf-Uskoplje, Marko Juric. For a long time, there were suspicions that this was carried out by members of the Patriotic League. It was only when they entered Kupres in 1994 was the situation clarified, and for that reason there was the fear that the Serbs might use this misunderstanding on our part and that we might be included in conflicts, but what we really needed to do was to strengthen our lines and defend Gornji Vakuf and Uskoplje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, according to my assumption, you explained that in June 1992, you had some of your comrades who were killed, and you believed for a long time that these were Muslims, and you discovered in 1994, when you entered Kupres, that, in fact, these were Serbs. Is that what you are telling us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that's what I wanted to say, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tokic, in the meantime my colleagues have told me that one of your answers was not recorded, so I'll repeat the question and ask you to repeat your answer. The question referred to the village of Zdrimci, Z-d-r-i-m-c-i, Zdrimci, and the question was whether, in that village, there were any members of the BH Army. So could you repeat your answer, please?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Counsel, in the village of Zdrimci, an infantry company was organised there of soldiers belonging to the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now let's look at the next document, which is 4D399, 399. It's a document dated November 1992. It is an order from Brigadier Milivoj Petkovic, and towards the end of that order he is instructing that they come into contact with the BH Army Command in Gornji Vakuf in order to overcome the mistrust, and to send units to the defence lines in Bugojno. Did you receive an order to that effect?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, did you carry it out?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Yes, in full. I acted upon it and ensured that the order was carried out.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: At that time, who was the commander of the BH Army in Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: The commander of the BH Army in Gornji Vakuf was Fahrudin Agic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Is that November 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: I'm not 100 per cent certain, but I think that in November Mr. Agic came and took up that post. But until October, it was Mr. Fikret Musa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: If you were to compare those two men, looking at their will to cooperate with the Croats and the HVO, who would you say was more cooperative?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Well, Fikret Musa, certainly, who, together with me, solved all the problems and incidents that broke out in the field.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right, thank you. Let's look at the next document briefly, please, P778. This is an exhibit already. I would like to briefly draw your attention to the following. It was a document produced by you, Mr. Tokic, about, as it says, a beastly murder of a Muslim citizen. In this letter, you address your colleagues from the BH Army to express your condolences, to apologise, and to point out that steps will be taken or have already been taken, judicial steps, against the perpetrator of this gruesome murder. Mr. Tokic, is this a document that you produced?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I will now be asking you several questions about raising combat readiness. To begin with, can we please look at 4D416, 4D416. This is an order by Colonel Siljeg, dated 9th of January, 1993, sent to all the operation zones' brigades. Mr. Tokic, did you, too, receive this order?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Item 1 is about combat readiness being raised, having received information that the Chetniks had brought reinforcements to certain sectors. Does that claim tally with what you knew at the time, Mr. Tokic?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Yes, fully.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In the introductory part of this order, Colonel Siljeg invokes an order by the Main Staff, numbered 33; is that right, Mr. Tokic?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. It says: "Pursuant to 01-33."

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's try to cross-reference this and find out what the document actually is. It's P1087, 1087, the Main Staff document, an order by Brigadier Petkovic, Chief of the Main Staff, dated the 9th of January. The filing number is the same; right?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Based on this document, what is your conclusion? Was it dispatched to all the operative zones or was it only dispatched about the incidents in Gornji Vakuf or the developments in Gornji Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: If we look closely, it was, in fact, dispatched to all operative zones.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. The next one up is 4D1403, the document issued by Arif Pasalic, the commander of the BH Army's 4th Corps. The date is the 3rd of January, 1993. If we look at the main body of the order, which is quite lengthy, we see that the BH Army has information indicating that the VRS is planning certain combat activities. For this reason, they are raising their own combat readiness and preparing for certain activities. We'll be looking at another document before I ask you a question about this. The next document is 4D394, again an Arif Pasalic document. The date is the 6th of January, 1993, taking measures to ensure maximum combat readiness in relation to the Geneva talks. In the penultimate paragraph, the document says it is to be expected that the aggressor will continue to try and score a military success, in relation to the talks, and also be stepping up combat activities. And then there are references to particular front-lines there. Mr. Tokic, what would seem to follow from this: Who is the aggressor, the VRS or another army?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Madam counsel, it is very clear, based on these documents, that the aggressor here is the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did you have any information indicating that the BH Army in Gornji Vakuf at the time were also stepping up their combat readiness because they expected activity on the part of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: I was all the time in touch with Mr. Agic. We knew about that, and we issued a joint order about what was to be done along the front-lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us try to briefly run through a couple of documents about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I have a technical question. The documents we saw show that the Serbs were listened -- were listened to by the HVO and the BH Army, because it's thanks to tapping that we learn that the Serbs probably intend to carry out an action in the Sector number 32, and obviously the HVO doesn't really know what "Sector 32" means. So given this, I'm wondering the following: I want to know whether you, in the HVO, were also eavesdropping on the BH Army and whether the BH Army was also tapping the HVO.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that was technically possible. Nevertheless, neither we, nor the army, were listening to each other. We were occupying a joint position along the front-line facing the VRS instead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're telling us that there was a technical possibility, but you did not do it, neither the HVO, nor the BH Army, because the both -- the both of you were siding against the Serbs; is that it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tokic, let's try and go back to 4D352 to check out two specific elements. This is a report from your own operative zone, the Gornji Vakuf. In the second sentence, we see the following: "Situation in the town in relation to the allies is still tense." Can you tell us who the reference is to, when the document says "the allies in Gornji Vakuf"?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Madam counsel, the BH Army units and no one but the BH Army units.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The next sentence reads: "The BH Army continues to deploy members of the BH Army from Jajce at several locations in the municipality." Mr. Tokic, was that actually the case?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether these developments to do with the Jajce Brigade affected the relations between the HVO and the BH Army in Vakuf?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Yes, to a large degree.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. Next one up, P1090, 1090, a collective --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, earlier you told us that the HVO and the BH Army were both facing the Serbs. I took due note of this. But this document, 4D452 [as interpreted] show that on the HVO side, there's concern. The HVO is finding out that the BH Army is deploying its troops in a number of settlements in this municipality, and the HVO, which has very good information, quotes three settlements, Voljevac, Podvode [phoen] and Voljice, where the BH Army deployed a number of men. For example, in Voljevac, there's 50 to 61 men led by a man known as Herman, a man who was already well known because he'd been involved in some kind of shady business earlier in 1983 or 1984, so there's elements for concern. Now, I'd like to know whether this was concerning enough to decide to take some steps against the BH Army, or whether these were just questions that the HVO had and nothing more at the time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this was a worrisome trend. I put in a word with the commander of the 317th Brigade, saying that the units were not originally from Gornji Vakuf and Uskoplje and that they could not be deployed in the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And what did your counterpart tell you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He told me that this was the 305th Jajce Brigade, commanded by Mr. Delic, and that about 600 of their men would be deployed in Croat-only areas and that they would not be sending 200 of them into Voljice until further notice. That was his plan, because Croats and Bosniaks were living together there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it might be a good idea to set the record straight immediately. We might be going back to that document. Page 27, line 9, that's one of your questions, you referred to 4D352, whereas the transcript reflects "4D452." So lest there be any confusion at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kovacic, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tokic, briefly on a number of other documents. P1090, a collective -- a consolidated report. The third paragraph from the bottom up reads, about your operative zone: Could you please comment on that? "On the part of the BH Army command staff, a warning arrived," a warning to the command of the HVO, "that no forces should be moving in motor vehicles around Gornji Vakuf municipality without previously obtaining approval from the 3rd Corps Command of the BH Army." Mr. Tokic, does this report tally with what you knew about the developments on the ground at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Madam counsel, yes, it does, fully.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The next one up, 4D354, 4D354, which is an order by Brigadier Milivoj Petkovic on the 11th of January, 1993, dispatching it to you, Mr. Tokic, requesting a report on the situation in Gornji Vakuf. Mr. Tokic, did you receive this order?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did you send back a report, pursuant to this order?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So what about the word "ally" in this document? Who is that a reference to?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: The BH Army units.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The next one up, 4D355, a report from your brigade, the 11th of January, sent to the Main Staff. Is that the report that was prepared based on Mr. Petkovic's order?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The next one up is P1101, 1101, likewise a consolidated report. The part that we're looking at is the one in relation to your own operative zone. It reads: "The commander of the Ante Starcevic Brigade received instructions to talk to the commanders," or, rather, "the commander of the BH Army for Gornji Vakuf, Agic, in order to try and allay the tensions and separate the warring sides, the flashing sides. Should he be unable to do that and as the situation dictates, he should move on with active defence activities." Mr. Tokic, did you really receive an order like this?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Would you look at the next document, please, P1115, P1115, an order by Brigadier Petkovic dated the 13th of January, 1993, saying that incidents should be avoided. The order was sent to Gornji Vakuf. My question, Mr. Tokic: Did you receive this order?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did you act on it?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Fully.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Next document, 4D356, 356, an interim report by Colonel Siljeg. The second part of the report says: "Passing through Vakuf and entering Vakuf, all blocked, they sealed off the Prozor-Bugojno road in the Drazov Dolac area, Duradbegov Dolac, Drasce, along the entrance to Gornji Vakuf, and our forces in the sectors of Humac, Pajic Polje, Mackovac, Hasici." Mr. Tokic, is the report accurate ? Was this really the case on the 13th of January?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. P --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, when reading this document, I note that a meeting was held in Gornji Vakuf between yourself and the commander of the BH Army, but there were also representatives of UNPROFOR. Do you remember this meeting attended also by representatives of UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do remember this meeting, and the meeting was, indeed, held at the UNPROFOR base in Gornji Vakuf-Uskoplje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the UNPROFOR was present. According to what you know, do you think that the UNPROFOR was trying to find out who was at the source of the incident, whether it was you or them? Did you feel monitored, did you feel like they were watching you, and that if you were doing something wrong, UNPROFOR would automatically find out -- find it out and tell everyone about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I did not have the feeling that I was being watched. I thought it was their duty to help us, and we truly wanted to resolve the whole situation in a peaceful way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document, P1131, is what I'd like to look at now. It's a report which was drafted by Miro Andric and Zeljko Siljeg, as well as Dr. Sandrk.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: From this report, which is already an exhibit, I'd just like to ask you to clarify one point. It says here: "Upon leaving Prozor, we were taken over by UN representatives and taken, in an APC, to the UN headquarters in Gornji Vakuf." Can you explain to us, Mr. Tokic, what this is all about?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Counsel, here it says -- well, none of the population or members of the HVO were able to enter Gornji Vakuf-Uskoplje in any other way, from the direction of Prozor, but in an armoured personnel carrier belonging to the UN. That was the only way you could do it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you explain to us when that became the situation and why?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Well, it was like that since the 9th of January because of the check-points that had been erected by the members of the BH Army by the fire brigade tower. Paraga, commander of the Green Berets, had simply blocked the main road, the M-16-2 main road at that point.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what year that was? The 9th of January, but what was the year?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the next document now, 4D343.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, this document states that an UNPROFOR soldier was killed by the sniper. Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do, Your Honour, and the Croatian Defence Council units -- well, we don't know how it actually happened, but, anyway, they simply sent their condolences to Major Jones and Colonel Stewart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But beyond the condolences, we still have an UNPROFOR soldier killed, and, a priori, he was killed by either one of the three parties, either the HVO, the BH Army, or the Serbs. As far as you know, could you tell us whether UNPROFOR was able to find out who -- where the shot came from, and, if they managed to do so, did they know who held that sector?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as far as I know, they didn't succeed in establishing with any certainty what happened here. I exclude the Army of Republika Srpska here because the incident took place on the bridge in the center of town, across the River Vrbas, at the separation line between the BH Army units and the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understand you correctly, the shot either came from the HVO or from the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tokic, tell us, was the HVO interested in having an investigation conducted and did it call for an investigation?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Counsel, the HVO did call for an investigation, and we offered to have some of our people included in that investigation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Was the proposal accepted?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: The proposal was accepted. However, the result -- the results of the investigation are not known.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the next document now, please, which is 4D343, and it's a combat report by the man on duty from your operative zone, and it refers to your brigade. It says: "In the area of responsibility of the Ante Starcevic Brigade, yesterday an agreement was reached on a cease-fire." And this is how that was put in place. There was sporadic fire from small arms throughout the night, and after the HVO stopped firing, the BH Army started regrouping its troops in several locations, along several axes, and other locations are mentioned where the most intensive regrouping was noticed. Does this description of events, to the best of your knowledge, Mr. Tokic, correspond to the situation on the ground or not?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does fully comply with the situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now let's look at the next document -- Your Honour, it seems that it's time for the break, so might we take the break now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's 10.30. We will break for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The next document, Mr. Tokic, is P1153, 1153. It's a set of instructions for further action which, on the 15th of January, 1993, was sent by Milivoj Petkovic to Gornji Vakuf. Tell me, Mr. Tokic, did you receive these instructions on the 15th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In your opinion, these instructions, can they be considered to be an order for attack?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Counsel, this can in no way be considered to be an order for attack.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, in the reference log-book, under what number was this order issued?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: The reference number is 01-67/93.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now look at the next document, which is P1139. It's an order from Brigadier Petkovic of the same day. The document is well known to everybody here in the courtroom. We know it as the order on re-subordination. Now, Mr. Tokic, did you receive this order?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: I never received an order like this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us under what number this order was issued? What's the reference number there?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: The reference number for this order is 01-70/93.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Tokic, we're going to discuss the matter of how the conflict was stopped. I'm skipping the conflict, itself, because General Praljak will be dealing with that - that was our agreement - but I'm going to show you three orders, first of all, all three, and then I'll ask you some questions. The first document is 1211, P1211 is the document number. It's an order from Mate Boban, dated the 19th of January, 1993, on forbidding any offensive action in Gornji Vakuf. The next document is P1238, 1238. It is also an order signed jointly by Milivoj Petkovic and Arif Pasalic, on the 20th of January, 1993, once again relating to a general cease-fire in Gornji Vakuf municipality. And the third document in that set is P1237, and that's an order from the Operative Zone of North-West Herzegovina, which follows on from the previous order signed by Pasalic and Petkovic. Now, tell us, Mr. Tokic, whether you received any of those three orders.

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Which?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: I received the order sent by Mr. Boban, and I received an order sent by Mr. Arif Pasalic and Brigadier Milivoj Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I see, fine. Now, tell us, did you act upon that order, did you carry it out?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Yes, fully.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And what about the BH Army, did it carry out Arif Pasalic's order?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Partially.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you explain what you mean when you say "partially"?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: The brigade commander, Mr. Agic, said that his troops, the troops that he commanded, accepted the order, but that there were certain forces that he was not in command and that he couldn't ensure that in such a short space of time the order is implemented.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now let's look at another set of orders on the same subject, and I'm going to show you three orders once again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a very short question of a technical nature. We have seen documents that ordered a cease-fire. At the head of the brigade, I assume that each soldier, perhaps not all of them had, but they all had a gun with ammunition. When there is a cease-fire, does the ammunition have to be handed back or are the soldiers entitled to keep their gun and their ammunition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the soldiers keep both their weapons and their ammunition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is always the case, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When an offensive is launched, one has a very reason to believe that enough and a large quantity of ammunition is needed. In that case, does the brigade command send out an order to say that each soldier needs to have enough ammunition or needs to have additional ammunition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If it's simply a case of preparation for some military action or defence, and if the unit does not have sufficient quantities of ammunition, then additional ammunition must be supplied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you supplement the ammunition, is an order sent out verbally or orally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, everybody communicating with the brigade commander must state their needs and requirements, and at the brigade headquarters all this is summarised and sent to the command for reinforcement and replenishment, because the brigade command does not have a logistics base.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as the logistical base is concerned that handles all the ammunition, there must be traces of when a given quantity of ammunition has been given to a given brigade, for instance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The command line makes sure there are records of how munition is used up, and then invoices [as interpreted] are signed, and based on this they know how much ammunition they distributed to each of the units on the ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My last question. As far as military techniques are concerned, if one wants a proof of an offensive, all one needs to do is look at the records of the logistical base to see whether such and such a unit has received additional ammunition; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because ammunition is used up equally for both attacking and defending.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies. Your Honours, while this is still on the screen, I think we should correct this. Page 37, line 21, it reads "and then invoices are signed." I think the witness said receipts, documents confirming receipt, but maybe the witness should tell us, himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you're right. Witness, these are receipts, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tokic, can we now please go to the next set of documents on how the clashes were stopped. The first one is P1286, which is an order by Brigadier Petkovic dated the 24th of January, 1993, from Geneva, on putting a stop to the clashes in Gornji Vakuf. The next document is P1300, an order by Colonel Siljeg, dated the 25th of January, on a cease-fire between the HVO and the BH Army. Colonel Siljeg invokes earlier instructions on the cease-fire, which we have discussed and which are referred to in the introductory part of the order. The fourth document is 4D346, the 25th of January, 1993, Colonel Siljeg. It's the same order for all HVO units to stop at the lines they had reached already, to continue to fortify their positions, and not to open fire first. Mr. Tokic, did you, at the time, receive any of these documents?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: I received all of these orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did you act on them?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Fully.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tokic, let's talk a little --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the last document, we see that groups of infantry infiltrated the area of Makljen. Who are these groups that infiltrated in Makljen?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may give the witness a hand, this is the end of paragraph 2 of 4D346.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, these are elements of BH Army units that simply tried to infiltrate themselves behind the lines of the Dr. Ante Starcevic Brigade units, their objective being to take the Makljen Pass and "ugrize" [as interpreted], the command post at Pidris.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Nozica [as interpreted], you have something like six to seven minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour. We're moving on now to a subject that will probably cause the greatest amount of interest on your part. I have to go through my documents swiftly. Can you please look at P1226, 1226. This document, the 3rd Corps commander, towards the very end of the document, says the population from the village of Uzricje moved out of their own volition, in part, and arrived in Gornji Vakuf, whereas the population of the village of Hrasnica was evacuated to Grnica. Does this report tally with the actual situation on the ground?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now on to P1210, another document by the BH Army. Paragraph 1 reports that the BH Army has lost the village of Uzricje, Dusa, and the lower part of Hrasnica. Mr. Tokic, based on your knowledge, was the HVO fighting the BH Army in the localities invoked in this report?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Next document, P1333, a document that you issued on the 27th of January, 1993, Mr. Tokic. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's one of my documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In this document, you invoke two categories of men: soldiers and civilians. Two categories of persons, if you like: soldiers and civilians. In which of these two would you place the military recruits, specifically Muslim ones?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Madam counsel, under the JNA doctrine they would be categorised at soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You refer to the JNA doctrine. Which doctrine, exactly, do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Quite simply, the All-People's Defence doctrine from the previous state, the Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: That's what you studied and taught at secondary school; right?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The next one, P1636, 1636, 1636. This is a list of prisoners released from the Prozor Detention Unit. Could you tell us, by looking at their names, which unit these men belonged to?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: These soldiers belonged to BH Army units.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The next document, P1351, which is an exhibit; therefore, I will merely summarise what my question is about in relation to the villages that are important to us. Uzricje, it says, in relation to that village, these citizens are trying to remain in their own village, while refugee families are requiring to be evacuated. The village of Dusa, 70 civilians are there. They are no prisoners, and they wish to remain in their own village. Nevertheless, they first want to confer with their husbands, who are captured. I've just read out to you what the commission found. Do their findings tally with what you knew to be the situation that prevailed?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at P1373. I hope that this is not a classified document. Unfortunately, we have not been able to check, specifically. In relation to the third village, there is some information in this document. This is an UNPROFOR document, the village of Zdrimci. There are about 100 Muslims in the village, for the most part the elderly men, women, and children, all of them wishing to leave. Based on your information, would that be accurate in relation to Zdrimci village?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Yes, entirely accurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The next document, P134 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document, P1373, it says that the Muslim families that were forced to leave the area, well, that this was due to ethnic cleansing. This is what this UNPROFOR battalion states. What do you have to say to this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was personally present there on the ground with Mr. Agic, the commander. In order to be able to speak more freely, he spoke to all of the Bosniaks who were there at the time. Following these conversations, he said that, quite simply, most of the population was ready to leave the village. The HVO, he said, show allow them to simply leave. Therefore, I, as a unit commander, did not make that decision. I was not the one to decide whether they would stay or leave the village. All those who wanted to stay received every guarantee from us that they would be allowed to stay on and be safe. But I must repeat the decision was theirs and theirs alone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Ms. Alaburic, you have no time left, but just finish with your documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm not Senka Nozica. My name is Vesna Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: About this question put by Judge Antonetti, Mr. Tokic, based on what he has just read out to you, it would seem to follow that this was a BH Army report to the effect that people were being forced to leave?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Madam counsel, please allow me to repeat. We did not force anyone to leave. Quite the contrary, we encouraged them to stay on and guaranteed their safety. Their decision was simply to leave the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I have only two documents left to show you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Witness. I still have a question on this document, and it relates to the last paragraph on the previous page, the last three lines: "The local BiH command were reported to be demanding compensation in cash for all the Muslim families who have been forced to move as a result of ethnic cleansing." Are you saying that this is wrong, that the UNPROFOR report here is lying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not wish to say that the UNPROFOR report is lying. This report is based on requests made by the BH Army units, but it really depends on how the request was formulated. This is certainly not an UNPROFOR position officially on this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: That is precisely what I was trying to ask you, Mr. Tokic. The wording here is by the BH Army and not an unbiased UNPROFOR report. But you just answered that question, which makes it even better. The next one is 1344, document 1344, instructions signed by Brigadier Petkovic and dispatched to Colonel Siljeg to capture and arrest all Croatian extremists, and then further instructions follow on how to put the situation under control in order to ensure there was peace and order. Did this set of instructions ever reach you, Mr. Tokic?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. Now I think this is your last document in the binder, P2259. A single village remains for us to deal with in that municipality, but no documents have so far been provided in relation to that village. I'm talking about Hrasnica. This document is an agreement signed on the 10th of May, 1993. You are listed here as one of the co-signatories. Mr. Tokic, is that a fact?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In this document, we read that the inhabitants of Hrasnica are free to go about their farming work and that guarantees would be provided by both commanders in terms of the safety and protection of these citizens. Two policemen will be seconded from each, the BH Army and the HVO ranks, to protect these citizens. What about the part of Hrasnica known as Gurici? Who was constantly in control of that area and who was it who was keeping their units there throughout?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Madam counsel, I do need to clarify one thing. This document was created as a result of an incident committed by the BH Army on the road following the railway line to Pajic Polje. Nefir [phoen], himself, is saying that they were about to seal this road off. After the HVO men captured two members of the BH Army, I informed the BH Army commander about this, sent the two soldiers back to him, after which the agreement was reached. This is a fact. As for Hrasnica, or Gurici, as the area is marked on some maps, effective control was retained by the BH Army throughout, and there were Bosniaks living there.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tokic, and in point 2, when mention is made of the locals of Hrasnica, what ethnicity does that have in mind?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: It means persons of both ethnicities, both Bosniaks and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Tokic, finally, could you tell us, at the end of the conflict, the Croatian-Muslim conflict in March 1994, what was the total number of Croats expelled [as interpreted], and how many Muslims were expelled in total?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: It's very difficult today, from this vantage point, to go back in time and remember all the pointers, but in these conflicts 4.900 Croats were expelled and somewhere around 1.760, to the best of my recollections, that is, because I dealt with these figures while I was head of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: When you say "1.760," you omitted to tell us what ethnicity those people were. So could you tell us now who were those 1.760?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: 1.760 persons of Bosniak ethnicity, and 4.900 persons of Croatian ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now, if you place these figures and compare them to the overall population of Croats and Muslims, could you give us the percentages, what percentage of people who left were Croatian and what percentage Muslim?

utterances.speaker: ZRINKO TOKIC
utterances.text: Well, there were about 25 per cent Croats and approximately 12 per cent Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Tokic. That completes my examination-in-chief, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before I give the floor to the Praljak Defence, one last follow-up question. The last document you signed, I see that the international representatives, Mr. Binns and Watkins, also signed the document. Do you remember how this all happened? Did you and your counterpart ask them to initial the document, or did they tell you that they had initialled the document? Do you remember how this happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, two soldiers of the BH Army were captured, and I informed the commander of the 317th, Mr. Emil Zejnilagic, about that. After that, we agreed that we should have a lasting, permanent document to secure peace in the area, and that those who wanted to could cultivate their land freely. As we, ourselves, did not wield sufficient authority with the other side, that is to say, I with the Bosniaks and he with the Croats, didn't have enough clout, we asked for somebody to act as mediator, somebody who enjoyed that authority, and we agreed that that kind of authority was vested in UNPROFOR, and we asked that a meeting of this kind be convened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I just intervene with respect to the transcript, and I thank Ms. Tomanovic for drawing our attention to that. On page 45, line 11, the term "expelled" was used, which can lead to misunderstandings over the meaning of my question, because I wanted to use neutral terms without entering into any violent expulsion concepts or whatever. So I was talking about people who left the territory of Gornji Vakuf, because at that point I didn't find it necessary to examine the conditions and circumstances under which the people left Gornji Vakuf. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
